content.title: About
content.content: Canned sardines are small oily fish, usually Sardina pilchardus, that are cleaned, lightly salted and then packed in oil or their own juice in a sealed can. The product retains a high level of protein, omega‑3 fatty acids and B‑vitamins, and it stores well for long periods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sardines are often called “the little fish with big benefits” because of their nutritional value.
Traditionally they are canned in olive oil, which enhances flavor and preserves healthy fats.
Sardines are one of the most affordable sources of omega‑3 worldwide.
In ancient Rome, sardines were already preserved in vinegar for consumption.
A can of sardines is a common “first‑aid” food for hikers and emergency kits.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids support heart health, reduce inflammation, and promote brain function.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A typical serving (about 30 g) provides roughly 6 g of complete protein needed for tissue repair and growth.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and supports the immune system.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Sardines with bones are a good source of calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Beta‑carotene and vitamin B12
items.content: These nutrients help energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned sardines often contain high levels of salt; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to seafood may experience reactions.

items.title: Contaminants
items.content: In rare cases, fish can accumulate heavy metals; choose reputable brands.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned sardines can be eaten straight from the can, added to salads, pasta, sandwiches, or used in spreads. They pair well with lemon, fresh herbs, and whole‑grain foods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct light. After opening, keep the sardines in a sealed container in the refrigerator and consume within 2‑3 days.
